resumen: Standing facing a high pulley, you bring a bar down to your thighs with the arms almost straight, moving only at the shoulders. It works the lats and the biceps barely takes part.
ejecucion: Grip the high pulley bar overhand, shoulder-width apart, and step back.
Lean your torso slightly forward with a straight back, arms almost straight in front of you.
Bring the bar down in an arc to your thighs, with your elbows fixed and slightly bent.
Return under control until your arms are at head height, without bending your elbows.
If your elbows bend to bring the bar down, you are doing a pulldown: lower the weight.
matices: With the elbows fixed, the motion is only at the shoulder, so the biceps barely takes part. How much the lats work compared with the chest has not been measured in this exercise; in the pullover, a similar movement, the chest came out ahead.
